chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the man who is seized and upon him are penalties, one of which is killing.
So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Ali (peace be upon him) used to establish the penalties upon him, then he would kill him, and Ali (peace be upon him) will not be opposed.'
ai.seo_question: How does Imam Ali handle multiple penalties when one is death?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the judicial precedent of Imam Ali (peace be upon him) in executing multiple hudud penalties sequentially, culminating in execution when one penalty is death. This practice underscores the principle of cumulative justice in Shia fiqh, ensuring that all prescribed punishments are fulfilled rather than subsumed by the most severe one. It highlights the practical application of prophetic tradition in early Islamic governance, affirming the authority of the Imam in administering comprehensive legal retribution.
